title: The Lost Dog
synopsis: Saturday morning. A small wet dog on your porch with no tags. The rain isn't stopping.

nodes.text: He shivers at the door. He doesn't try to come in. Inside is already waiting. What changes is whether “Open the door” or “Bring a towel out” is the instinct you carry into it.

choices.consequence: You open the door. The decision moves you toward Inside and tells everyone present what you are willing to risk.
You commit to bring a towel out. By Inside, the choice has already shifted who trusts you and who begins to watch.

nodes.text: He sleeps on your old hoodie within twelve minutes. The Walk will follow either decision, but it will meet a different version of you after “Post photos online” than after “Knock door to door.”

choices.consequence: You choose to post photos online. It opens the route to The Walk, giving up the protection of pretending you had not decided.
You knock door to door. The decision moves you toward The Walk and tells everyone present what you are willing to risk.

nodes.text: Nobody recognizes him. A woman crosses herself. A kid hugs his neck. Both choices lead to Chip, but “Try the vet” arrives there with a different cost than “Try the shelter.”

choices.consequence: You choose to try the vet. It opens the route to Chip, giving up the protection of pretending you had not decided.
You try the shelter. The decision moves you toward Chip and tells everyone present what you are willing to risk.

nodes.text: The vet finds a chip. The owner moved out of state last year and didn't update. You cannot avoid She Calls Back; you can only decide whether “Try to reach her anyway” or “Foster him for now” defines the person who reaches it.

choices.consequence: You try to reach her anyway. The decision moves you toward She Calls Back and tells everyone present what you are willing to risk.
You commit to foster him for now. By She Calls Back, the choice has already shifted who trusts you and who begins to watch.

nodes.text: She is on the phone crying. He has been missing for fourteen months. Reunion will follow either decision, but it will meet a different version of you after “Offer to drive” than after “Offer to ship him properly.”

choices.consequence: You choose to offer to drive. It opens the route to Reunion, giving up the protection of pretending you had not decided.
You offer to ship him properly. The decision moves you toward Reunion and tells everyone present what you are willing to risk.

nodes.text: She kneels on her driveway. He runs in a straight line. The distance between A Postcard, Every Month and Foster Fail begins with the choice between “Stay for tea” and “Drive home content.”

choices.consequence: You choose to stay for tea. It opens the route to A Postcard, Every Month, giving up the protection of pretending you had not decided.
You drive home content. The decision moves you toward Foster Fail and tells everyone present what you are willing to risk.

nodes.text: She sends you postcards forever. You frame the first one. The road into A Postcard, Every Month began with “Stay for tea” in Reunion; here, that decision stops being a moment and becomes a life.

You almost gave him up. You almost did. The almost was a long second. The road into Foster Fail began with “Drive home content” in Reunion; here, that decision stops being a moment and becomes a life.
